scenes.title: 1974 North Vancouver Outdoor Gorge: 230-Foot Swaying Capilano Suspension Bridge vs 10-Foot Solid Cedar Bridge
scenes.era: 1974, Capilano Canyon Suspension Bridge, North Vancouver, British Columbia

layout.description: Sunlit Pacific Northwest cedar-forest gorge spanned by the narrow 450-foot swaying wooden-plank and steel-cable suspension bridge 230 feet above churning whitewater rapids, where a female UBC researcher hands a torn paper contact slip to a traveler gripping the wire cable.

positions.who: Female UBC interviewer (in 1974 corduroy jacket over knit turtleneck holding wooden clipboard)
positions.where: standing mid-span on the swaying cedar planks tearing the top-right phone-number corner off a questionnaire sheet
positions.facing: angled toward the arriving traveler mid-bridge

positions.who: 38-year-old male traveler (in 1974 nylon windbreaker and denim, one hand gripping the steel handrail cable)
positions.where: glancing down at the 230-foot canyon drop with chest rising rapidly before smiling warmly as he accepts the paper slip
positions.facing: facing the interviewer mid-span on the suspension bridge

props.name: swaying cedar-plank suspension bridge deck and steel handrail cable
props.period_detail: 1974 Capilano 5-foot-wide, 230-foot-high gorge span contrasting against the solid 10-foot creek bridge
props.physical_behavior: State-A wooden planks tilt gently over whitewater gorge as traveler grips steel cable tightly -> State-B traveler steadies stance leaning in attentively toward interviewer

props.name: wooden research clipboard and torn paper phone-number corner slip
props.period_detail: exact 1974 JPSP dependent measure tracking voluntary post-bridge phone calls (50.0% vs 12.5%)
props.physical_behavior: State-A interviewer tears paper corner cleanly from clipboard sheet -> State-B traveler tucks paper slip carefully into jacket pocket

actions.verb_sequence: steadies one hand on the swaying steel bridge cable as his pulse races -> takes the torn paper slip from the interviewer and tucks it straight into his breast pocket
presents the picture card on her clipboard, tears off the contact corner, and hands it across the swaying span

reactions.reaction: bright, captivated grin mistaking canyon adrenaline for instant interpersonal spark
neutral, professional nod keeping script identical across both bridges

scenes.wardrobe: 1974 Pacific Northwest outdoor wear: rust nylon windbreaker, plaid flannel shirt, corduroy jacket, and denim.
scenes.lighting: Crisp sunlit evergreen-canyon daylight above bright whitewater spray.
scenes.recognition_hook: Meet on a sturdy 10-foot creek bridge and 12.5% call; meet 230 feet up a swaying gorge bridge and 50.0% dial the number.

key_visual.description: a sunlit forest canyon suspension bridge high above rapids where a researcher with a wooden clipboard hands a torn paper slip to a traveler gripping the steel cable

scenes.title: Study 2 Cedar Park Bench 10 Minutes Past the Bridge Exit: Cooled Pulse Halves the Spark
scenes.era: 1974, shaded cedar park bench beyond the Capilano bridge exit

layout.description: Peaceful dappled-sunlight park clearing ten minutes past the suspension bridge exit with a solid cedar bench.

positions.where: conversing calmly beside the cedar bench ten minutes after crossing once breathing and pulse have returned to resting baseline
positions.facing: standing calmly beside shaded park bench

props.name: solid cedar park bench and stainless wristwatch
props.period_detail: Dutton & Aron Study 2 10-minute post-crossing heart-rate recovery window
props.physical_behavior: State-A traveler sits resting hands on knees for 10 minutes as chest breathing slows -> State-B accepts paper slip casually with half the callback urgency (30% vs 65%)

actions.verb_sequence: rests ten minutes on the cedar bench until pulse cools, glances calmly at the clipboard, and walks on unhurriedly

reactions.reaction: friendly but unhurried composure once canyon adrenaline fades

scenes.recognition_hook: Same thrill-seekers, same scary bridge—waiting ten minutes on a park bench for their pulse to cool cut phone calls from 65% to 30%.

scenes.title: Long-Term Couple Shared Adventure Overlook: Using Excitation Transfer Together on Purpose

layout.description: Sunlit coastal wooden overlook trail where a 55-year-old married couple finishes an invigorating climb together.

positions.where: laughing warmly together at the sunlit scenic railing with energized posture after completing a brisk new trail
positions.facing: sharing a warm look beside coastal wooden railing

props.name: two lightweight hiking poles and insulated trail thermos
props.period_detail: Arthur Aron's long-term couple shared-novelty takeaway
props.physical_behavior: State-A couple props hiking poles against overlook rail -> State-B clasp hands warmly sharing energized post-climb laughter

actions.verb_sequence: leans hiking poles against the wooden overlook rail and clasps hands laughing as shared healthy excitement boosts warmth

scenes.wardrobe: Modern breathable outdoor fleece jackets and trail shirts.
scenes.recognition_hook: Sharing a novel, heart-pumping activity with your long-term partner channels healthy adrenaline straight into renewed closeness.
